measured.the_irony: the pin BOUND CORRECTLY - the low instruction was in the served prompt because --default-chat-template-kwargs worked; the gate asserted SILENCE (the medium arm's neutrality signature) instead of the REQUESTED value's signature
measured.root_cause: serve-defs constant Q38_EFFORT was frozen at 'medium' by the one-variable proof itself: q38_arm_diff.py enforced byte-identity of cell 8 modulo only the chat-template-kwargs literal, which LOCKED the certification logic to the old arm's semantics

why_informative: This null rules out nothing about the mechanism (no game was played) but establishes an instrument-discipline finding: a one-variable proof that freezes verification logic across arms converts a correct poisoning gate into a landmine, because a gate's EXPECTED VALUES are a function of the variable while its LOGIC must be invariant. Fix shipped and negative-controlled: certification is now arm-aware (assert the requested value's marker, never silence), the arm-diff normalises declared arm-dependent tokens and asserts each arm's constant is correct, and a replay reproduces this exact death as a permanent regression test. Secondary finding: the pin mechanism (server default_chat_template_kwargs merge) is CONFIRMED WORKING in production for a second value ('low'), which the medium arm alone could not establish.
